column3: Engineered biomimetic materials for intestinal mucosal healing (Transfer)
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEDespite advances in available treatment achieving mucosal healing remains challenging for many patientssuffering from inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). In this proposal we will engineer a biomaterial-basedbiomimetic system that can selectively target the inflamed mucosa and locally release therapeutics to thedamaged epithelium. The proposed research will use innovative approaches that employ drug delivery not onlymimicking the mucus layer but also as a tool to interrogate epithelial repair at the site of mucosal inflammationto shed light on mechanisms of mucosal healing for IBD and many other mucosal barrier disorders.

column3: Hydrogel Delivery of Bacteriophage to Treat Wound Infections
column4: Project NarrativeBacteriophages viruses that kill bacteria are a promising but currently inadequate solution to the problem ofmultidrug-resistant bacterial infections. These studieshave the potential to transform the treatment of chronic multidrug-resistant bacterial infections.

column3: Single stage surgical intervention for treatment of severe traumatic brain injury
column4: NarrativeWhen someone suffers a severe brain injury a portion of the skull must be removed so that the brain can swell.Unfortunately a second surgery is required to replace that missing piece of the skull and the patient canexperience neurological problems up until the day that missing bone is replaced. In a rat model we believe thatplacing our new flexible material during the first surgery that can later turn into bone will still allow the brain toswell initially while avoiding the second surgery and the neurological problems.

column3: Enhanced Delivery of Cytotoxic Neural Stem Cells for Treatment of Glioblastoma Multiforme Using an Innovative In-situ Thermogelling Hydrogel and Focused Ultrasound
column4: RELEVANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTHThe benefit of effective and less invasive therapies that can replace invasive surgical procedures and enhancetreatment outcomes for glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) patients is significant. Biomaterial formulations providingsteady and prolonged release over several months of highly effective tumor homing killer cells known as neuralstem cells (NSCs) and the use of a non-invasive dosing method known as focused ultrasound (FUS) to deliverNSCs systemically and across the blood brain barrier (BBB) can potentially increase efficacy outcomes to GBMtreatment regimen and transform the GBM treatment landscape. The overarching goal of this proposal is todevelop and evaluate a new treatment modality that combines a biodegradable and highly tunable biomaterialscaffold and non-invasive FUS to enhance delivery of NSCs to tumor cells and to curb the treatment of GBM.

column3: Self-Assembling Camptothecin Nanofiber Hydrogels as Adjunct Therapy for Intraoperative Treatment of Malignant Glioma
column4: Project narrative (relevance)One of the greatest hurdles to prolonging survival in patients with malignant brain tumors is the inevitable tumorrecurrence in the vicinity of the original location or the resection cavities despite multimodal treatment includingsurgery radiotherapy and chemotherapy. We aim to develop a camptothecin drug amphiphile (DA)nanofiber hydrogel platform technology as adjunct therapy for intraoperative treatment of malignant braincancer that can eradicate infiltrated glioma cells by maintaining a therapeutic concentration within the brain whileminimizing systemic drug exposure. This goal will be achieved by evaluating and optimizing our current hydrogel-forming DA technology with in vitro ex vivo and in vivo brain tumor models well-established in our laboratoryand the results of our study will validate a new local treatment strategy to combat currently incurable braincancers with significant survival benefits and good tolerance.

column3: Drug delivery platform for ocular allergy therapy
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEAmong the estimated 165 million worldwide contact lens wearers approximately one third of these suffer fromallergies but face a challenge as the application of eye drops is generally incompatible with lens wearing. Wepropose to develop a next generation 1-day drug delivery contact lens (DDCL) for olopatadine using boundarycharge modifiers to extend and control drug release the work will build on the Lynthera project team's previousaccomplishments in the field  enabling the use of the most efficacious allergy drug and the most popular contactlens material (silicone hydrogel). A daily disposable DDCL with prescription and loaded with olopatadine cansustainably deliver high-precision dosage for at least 12 hours to relieve allergy symptoms.

column3: Dynamic Acellular Materials for Repairing Dense Connective Tissues
column4: NarrativeMenisci of the knee cushion our joints during normal loading but are commonly injured. Unfortunately healing ofmenisci in adults is limited and current treatments do not restore function resulting in degeneration of theunderlying cartilage and progressive joint disease. To address this we engineer injectable biomaterials withtailored biofactor release to sequentially promote cell migration from surrounding tissue and direct matrixformation upon arrival at the injury site and test these in a clinically relevant large animal meniscus repair model.

column3: Optimizing Therapeutic Revascularization by  Endothelial Cell_Transplantation
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEAs in the parent grant the supplement address a problem that is common to tissue engineering of allvascularized replacement organs namely how to incorporate a functional microvascular system for organperfusion. We will introduce two new innovations in this supplement: (1) we will use a new versatile degradablepolymer material for delivery of growth factors particularly VEGF in a time and spatially controlled fashionwithin our 3D bioprinted skin; and (2) we will use an innovative strategy for controlled slow extracellularrelease of mRNA polyplexes which will allow us to provide weeks long expression of mRNA creatingprolonged Bcl2 expression (which we have previously show to dramatically enhance vascular maturation)providing safer more transient expression than is possible with viral vectors.

column3: Catheter-injectable engineered biomaterial for sustained Neuregulin-1 delivery to the myocardium
column4: Project NarrativeNeuregulin-1 (NRG1) is a promising recombinant protein therapy for myocardial infarction (MI) which like mostprotein therapies suffers from rapid loss of function during conventional intravenous administrationnecessitating high dosing repeated administration and/or long treatment periods. In this study we present thedevelopment and evaluation of a new engineered injectable liposome-crosslinked hydrogel for sustained NRG1delivery into infarcted myocardium. Success of this proposed study would enhance the outcomes of NRG1therapy for MI and provide a novel approach for sustained direct delivery of therapeutics into the heart.

column3: A Relaxin-loaded Hydrogel for the Treatment of Hypertrophic Scars
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEHypertrophic scars arise in over 50% of all surgical procedures and 90% of burn injuries and are physicallyuncomfortable and painful as well as inflict psychological damage due to their negative cosmetic appearances.Current treatment options are limited in their scope and efficacy as they do not target the underlying cause ofscar development: a dysregulated wound healing response. Here the sustained and localized delivery of thenatural antifibrotic peptide hormone relaxin-2 via a hydrogel is described as a novel solution to treat both theunderlying etiology and symptomatic presentation of hypertrophic scars.

column3: Engineering the open porous nanofibrous microsphere integrated fibrillar hydrogel for the co-delivery of antibacterial and angiogenic agents aimed at the rapid diabetic wound repair
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEPreventing infections vascularization cell migration and reintegration with surrounding tissues are vital factorsin diabetic wound healing. Here we propose to develop an extracellular matrix (ECM) mimicking porousnanofibrous microspheres (NMs) integrated with fibrillar hydrogel to co-deliver both antibacterial and angiogenicpeptides to the wound site to control infections and enhance vascularization during the diabetic wound healing.The novel open porous architecture of the NMs facilitates rapid cell migration and accelerates the healingprocess; thus our goal is to engineer an inexpensive effective and minimally invasive combinatorial treatmentstrategy to treat diabetic wounds.

column3: Engineered biomaterials for promoting lymphatic regeneration in lymphedema
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEThis proposed study aims to leverage biomaterial and drug delivery methodologies to achieve two primaryobjectives: firstly to augment lymphatic regeneration by integrating hydrogels that promote lymphatic growthwith vascularized lymph node transfer (VLNT) and secondly to encourage lymphatic vessel expansion at sitedistal to the original lymphatic injury using drug delivery to the lymphatics. column3: Drug eluting injectable biomaterials for next generation chemoembolization
column4: NarrativeThe 5-year survival rate of liver cancer patients is as low as 9.9% in the United States and 6.2% in Europe.Nearly 2 billion people worldwide infected with hepatic viral diseases are at risk for developing liver cancerand dying owing to limited therapeutic options. While historically systemic chemotherapy has been thecornerstone to cancer treatment inability to achieve uniform drug delivery to tumors collateral toxicity to non-cancerous liver and systemic side-effects have limited progress in the development of novel therapies for livercancer. We propose a transformative platform technology that uses a catheter based locoregionalapproach to deliver X-ray visible bioengineered biomaterial i.e. next generation TACE to induce a moreefficient ischemic cell death within the tumor microvasculature that can be coupled with chemo- andimmunotherapy. We believe that our approach will prevent progression of cancer providing time to bridgemore patients to the curative liver transplantation and extend lives.

column3: SynerGel: A Novel Tumor Microenvironment-Modulating Hydrogel for Local Immunotherapy
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVE.The overall 5-year survival rate for head and neck cancer has not improved much over the last few decades withboth conventional multimodal treatment and emerging immunotherapies known to have an adverse (andsometimes fatal) impact on quality of life. The goal of this proposal is to investigate the mechanisms driving theeffectiveness of a novel immunotherapy for head and neck cancer we call SynerGel and determine how it canbe used in combination with standard-of-care radiation therapy to reduce treatment toxicity. By doing so we aimto enhance our understanding of how both tumor and immune cells in the tumor environment can be manipulatedto produce a strong anti-tumor effect while reducing the side effects of treatment.

column4: Project narrativeIn the United States 1.84 million people have type 1 diabetes with 21% increase in diagnosis between 2001and 2009 and 5 million people expected to be diagnosed by 2050. Islet transplantation can cure type 1diabetes but it requires chronic systemic immunosuppression which limits the applicability of this procedureonly to the most severe cases of type 1 diabetes. Our innovative platform for islet microencapsulation throughconformal coating combined with our localized immunomodulatory approaches may eliminate the need forlifelong systemic immunosuppression and extend the applicability of islet transplantation to a larger number ofpatients with type 1 diabetes.

column3: Nanobarrier contact lenses for mono and combination therapy for treating microbial keratitis
column4: Microbial keratitis (MK) therapy by eye drops has many deficiencies including high frequency dosing and low dose deliveryto target tissues of about 1-5%. We propose to develop drug eluting contact lenses capable of delivering about 50% doseto target tissues allowing replacement of tedious drop therapy involving multiple drops each day with the use of a singlecontact lens for 3-days therapy followed by another lens for 3-days if needed. The proposed research aims to manufactureand characterize novel nanobarrier lenses and measure in vivo drug release and efficacy in an animal model.

column3: Enhanced Delivery of Cytotoxic Neural Stem Cells for Treatment of Glioblastoma Multiforme Using an Innovative In-situ Thermogelling Hydrogel and Focused Ultrasound
column4: RELEVANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTHThe benefit of effective and less invasive therapies that can replace invasive surgical procedures and enhancetreatment outcomes for glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) patients is significant. Biomaterial formulations providingsteady and prolonged release over several months of highly effective tumor homing killer cells known as neuralstem cells (NSCs) and the use of a non-invasive dosing method known as focused ultrasound (FUS) to deliverNSCs systemically and across the blood brain barrier (BBB) can potentially increase efficacy outcomes to GBMtreatment regimen and transform the GBM treatment landscape. The overarching goal of this proposal is todevelop and evaluate a new treatment modality that combines a biodegradable and highly tunable biomaterialscaffold and non-invasive FUS to enhance delivery of NSCs to tumor cells and to curb the treatment of GBM.

column4: Project narrative (relevance)One of the greatest hurdles to prolonging survival in patients with malignant brain tumors is the inevitable tumorrecurrence in the vicinity of the original location or the resection cavities despite multimodal treatment includingsurgery radiotherapy and chemotherapy. We aim to develop a camptothecin drug amphiphile (DA)nanofiber hydrogel platform technology as adjunct therapy for intraoperative treatment of malignant braincancer that can eradicate infiltrated glioma cells by maintaining a therapeutic concentration within the brain whileminimizing systemic drug exposure. This goal will be achieved by evaluating and optimizing our current hydrogel-forming DA technology with in vitro ex vivo and in vivo brain tumor models well-established in our laboratoryand the results of our study will validate a new local treatment strategy to combat currently incurable braincancers with significant survival benefits and good tolerance.

column3: A Relaxin-loaded Hydrogel for the Treatment of Hypertrophic Scars
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEHypertrophic scars arise in over 50% of all surgical procedures and 90% of burn injuries and are physicallyuncomfortable and painful as well as inflict psychological damage due to their negative cosmetic appearances.Current treatment options are limited in their scope and efficacy as they do not target the underlying cause ofscar development: a dysregulated wound healing response. Here the sustained and localized delivery of thenatural antifibrotic peptide hormone relaxin-2 via a hydrogel is described as a novel solution to treat both theunderlying etiology and symptomatic presentation of hypertrophic scars.

column3: Drug eluting injectable biomaterials for next generation chemoembolization
column4: NarrativeThe 5-year survival rate of liver cancer patients is as low as 9.9% in the United States and 6.2% in Europe.Nearly 2 billion people worldwide infected with hepatic viral diseases are at risk for developing liver cancerand dying owing to limited therapeutic options. While historically systemic chemotherapy has been thecornerstone to cancer treatment inability to achieve uniform drug delivery to tumors collateral toxicity to non-cancerous liver and systemic side-effects have limited progress in the development of novel therapies for livercancer. We propose a transformative platform technology that uses a catheter based locoregionalapproach to deliver X-ray visible bioengineered biomaterial i.e. next generation TACE to induce a moreefficient ischemic cell death within the tumor microvasculature that can be coupled with chemo- andimmunotherapy. We believe that our approach will prevent progression of cancer providing time to bridgemore patients to the curative liver transplantation and extend lives.

column3: Injectable Hydrogels to Deliver Gene Therapy for Myocardial Infarct
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVE Myocardial infarction (MI) is a leading cause of death in the US. While growth factor-encoding genes isa promising therapy for MI local delivery remains an unmet challenge due to poor injectability of gene carriersand low payload retention within the beating heart. We propose the design of an injectable biomaterial thataddresses these two specific challenges: first the gel undergoes dynamic crosslinking to facilitate minimallyinvasive catheter delivery; second the gel rapidly and robustly self-heals to localize therapeutic genes within thecontracting myocardium; thus enabling the clinical translation of gene-based MI therapies.

column4: Project narrative (relevance)One of the greatest hurdles to prolonging survival in patients with malignant brain tumors is the inevitable tumorrecurrence in the vicinity of the original location or the resection cavities despite multimodal treatment includingsurgery radiotherapy and chemotherapy. We aim to develop a camptothecin drug amphiphile (DA)nanofiber hydrogel platform technology as adjunct therapy for intraoperative treatment of malignant braincancer that can eradicate infiltrated glioma cells by maintaining a therapeutic concentration within the brain whileminimizing systemic drug exposure. This goal will be achieved by evaluating and optimizing our current hydrogel-forming DA technology with in vitro ex vivo and in vivo brain tumor models well-established in our laboratoryand the results of our study will validate a new local treatment strategy to combat currently incurable braincancers with significant survival benefits and good tolerance.

column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEPreventing infections vascularization cell migration and reintegration with surrounding tissues are vital factorsin diabetic wound healing. Here we propose to develop an extracellular matrix (ECM) mimicking porousnanofibrous microspheres (NMs) integrated with fibrillar hydrogel to co-deliver both antibacterial and angiogenicpeptides to the wound site to control infections and enhance vascularization during the diabetic wound healing.The novel open porous architecture of the NMs facilitates rapid cell migration and accelerates the healingprocess; thus our goal is to engineer an inexpensive effective and minimally invasive combinatorial treatmentstrategy to treat diabetic wounds.

column3: Designing non-toxic hydrogels for trans-tympanic drug delivery and treatment of otitis media
column4: This project aims to create a new non-toxic drug delivery hydrogel to directly and non-invasivelytreat acute otitis media (OM) a disease that affects 95% of US children. The proposal builds onprevious research showing successful eradication of OM using polymeric hydrogels by employingsolely chemistries approved by the FDA for topical oral and intravenous delivery which in theshort term can accelerate downstream clinical translation to improve child health. In the long termthis one-application direct delivery system has the potential to reduce treatment side effects curbantimicrobial resistance and improve treatment access and efficacy by removing barriers topatient compliance associated with oral therapy.

column3: Therapeutic bubble tea: Preventing the formation of uremic toxins with hydrogel immobilized microbes
column4: Project narrativeIt is proposed that by lowering indole and p-cresol in the intestines the formation of indoxylsulfate and p-cresol sulfate in the liver can be reduced hence lowering two important protein-bound uremic retention solutes that otherwise cannot be efficiently removed with dialysis. Wewill utilize polymer and hydrogel engineering to tailor hydrogel beads that can be ingested asbubble teas and later be excreted intact from the GI tract. column3: Preventive and Therapeutic Effects of Bone Marrow Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes on Spine Dural Fibrosis
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVE Spinal dural fibrosis including epidural and peridural fibrosis is defined as non-physiologic scar formation andis the most common cause of failed back surgery syndrome which refers to a cluster of symptoms in spinal cordand nerve roots after spinal surgery. If not properly treated the dural fibrosis can generally worsen which mayrequire surgical treatments including percutaneous adhesiolysis and spinal endoscopy however success ofthese surgical interventions is only 30-35%. Thus there is a critical and urgent need to develop pharmacologicaltherapies of dural fibrosis and we propose mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes have the potential toprevent and treat spinal dural fibrosis driven by active myofibroblasts.

column3: Drug eluting injectable biomaterials for next generation chemoembolization
column4: NarrativeThe 5-year survival rate of liver cancer patients is as low as 9.9% in the United States and 6.2% in Europe.Nearly 2 billion people worldwide infected with hepatic viral diseases are at risk for developing liver cancerand dying owing to limited therapeutic options. While historically systemic chemotherapy has been thecornerstone to cancer treatment inability to achieve uniform drug delivery to tumors collateral toxicity to non-cancerous liver and systemic side-effects have limited progress in the development of novel therapies for livercancer. We propose a transformative platform technology that uses a catheter based locoregionalapproach to deliver X-ray visible bioengineered biomaterial i.e. next generation TACE to induce a moreefficient ischemic cell death within the tumor microvasculature that can be coupled with chemo- andimmunotherapy. We believe that our approach will prevent progression of cancer providing time to bridgemore patients to the curative liver transplantation and extend lives.

column3: Injectable Hydrogels to Deliver Gene Therapy for Myocardial Infarct
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVE Myocardial infarction (MI) is a leading cause of death in the US. While growth factor-encoding genes isa promising therapy for MI local delivery remains an unmet challenge due to poor injectability of gene carriersand low payload retention within the beating heart. column4: NarrativeThe 5-year survival rate of liver cancer patients is as low as 9.9% in the United States and 6.2% in Europe.Nearly 2 billion people worldwide infected with hepatic viral diseases are at risk for developing liver cancerand dying owing to limited therapeutic options. While historically systemic chemotherapy has been thecornerstone to cancer treatment inability to achieve uniform drug delivery to tumors collateral toxicity to non-cancerous liver and systemic side-effects have limited progress in the development of novel therapies for livercancer. We propose a transformative platform technology that uses a catheter based locoregionalapproach to deliver X-ray visible bioengineered biomaterial i.e. next generation TACE to induce a moreefficient ischemic cell death within the tumor microvasculature that can be coupled with chemo- andimmunotherapy. We believe that our approach will prevent progression of cancer providing time to bridgemore patients to the curative liver transplantation and extend lives.

column3: Injectable Hydrogels to Deliver Gene Therapy for Myocardial Infarct
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVE Myocardial infarction (MI) is a leading cause of death in the US. While growth factor-encoding genes isa promising therapy for MI local delivery remains an unmet challenge due to poor injectability of gene carriersand low payload retention within the beating heart. We propose the design of an injectable biomaterial thataddresses these two specific challenges: first the gel undergoes dynamic crosslinking to facilitate minimallyinvasive catheter delivery; second the gel rapidly and robustly self-heals to localize therapeutic genes within thecontracting myocardium; thus enabling the clinical translation of gene-based MI therapies.

column4: PROJECT NARRATIVE Current therapies are unable to overcome the healing defects in severe burns underscoring the urgentneed for more effective therapies. column3: Drug eluting injectable biomaterials for next generation chemoembolization
column4: NarrativeThe 5-year survival rate of liver cancer patients is as low as 9.9% in the United States and 6.2% in Europe.Nearly 2 billion people worldwide infected with hepatic viral diseases are at risk for developing liver cancerand dying owing to limited therapeutic options. While historically systemic chemotherapy has been thecornerstone to cancer treatment inability to achieve uniform drug delivery to tumors collateral toxicity to non-cancerous liver and systemic side-effects have limited progress in the development of novel therapies for livercancer. We propose a transformative platform technology that uses a catheter based locoregionalapproach to deliver X-ray visible bioengineered biomaterial i.e. next generation TACE to induce a moreefficient ischemic cell death within the tumor microvasculature that can be coupled with chemo- andimmunotherapy. We believe that our approach will prevent progression of cancer providing time to bridgemore patients to the curative liver transplantation and extend lives.

column3: Injectable Hydrogels to Deliver Gene Therapy for Myocardial Infarct
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVE Myocardial infarction (MI) is a leading cause of death in the US. While growth factor-encoding genes isa promising therapy for MI local delivery remains an unmet challenge due to poor injectability of gene carriersand low payload retention within the beating heart. We propose the design of an injectable biomaterial thataddresses these two specific challenges: first the gel undergoes dynamic crosslinking to facilitate minimallyinvasive catheter delivery; second the gel rapidly and robustly self-heals to localize therapeutic genes within thecontracting myocardium; thus enabling the clinical translation of gene-based MI therapies.

column3: Regenerative Lipid Mediators for the Management of Severe Burn Wounds
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVE Current therapies are unable to overcome the healing defects in severe burns underscoring the urgentneed for more effective therapies. The successful completion of our proposed studies will provide: 1) a primaryhydrogel dressing that delivers regenerative lipid mediators (ReLiMs) and provides matrix and covering for theefficient healing of severe burn wounds; and 2) an innovative matrix that provides ReLiMs together with ReLiM-protected and guided uncultured adipose-tissue derived microvascular fragments for the more efficient healingof large deep burn wounds. These regenerative lipid mediator functionalized dressings with nonexistent orminimized graft-donor requirements are a promising adjuvant therapy to overcome the drawbacks of graftingmethods or skin substitutes currently used to treat severe burns.

column3: Regenerative Lipid Mediators for the Management of Severe Burn Wounds
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVE Current therapies are unable to overcome the healing defects in severe burns underscoring the urgentneed for more effective therapies. The successful completion of our proposed studies will provide: 1) a primaryhydrogel dressing that delivers regenerative lipid mediators (ReLiMs) and provides matrix and covering for theefficient healing of severe burn wounds; and 2) an innovative matrix that provides ReLiMs together with ReLiM-protected and guided uncultured adipose-tissue derived microvascular fragments for the more efficient healingof large deep burn wounds. While growth factor-encoding genes isa promising therapy for MI local delivery remains an unmet challenge due to poor injectability of gene carriersand low payload retention within the beating heart. We propose the design of an injectable biomaterial thataddresses these two specific challenges: first the gel undergoes dynamic crosslinking to facilitate minimallyinvasive catheter delivery; second the gel rapidly and robustly self-heals to localize therapeutic genes within thecontracting myocardium; thus enabling the clinical translation of gene-based MI therapies.

column4: Project NarrativeDespite advances in surgical techniques methods of radiation therapy and chemotherapeutic strategies theoverall 5-year survival rate for head and neck cancer has not improved much over the last few decades. Inaddition the potential morbidities associated with conventional multimodal treatment can have an adverseimpact on quality of life. The goal of this proposal is to investigate the mechanisms driving the surprisingeffectiveness of a novel immunotherapy for head and neck cancer we call STINGel. column3: Combined Hydrogel/Microparticle Eye Drops for Sustained Delivery of Glaucoma Medication
column4: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE:  Glaucoma is the second leading cause of blindness worldwide with this prevalence expected to increase substantially in coming years as it is more common in elderly adults.  The most common and preferred treatment to slow or stop the progression of glaucoma is the self-administration of topical eye drop medication as many as three times a day.  Eye drops are a highly inefficient treatment method due to limited retention and absorption of drug patient compliance issues due to the frequent dosing and side effects resulting from high levels of drug needed to achieve therapeutic effects.  Current efforts to develop new sustained release formulations that provide controlled delivery of glaucoma drugs for days or weeks (avoiding the need for topical drops) require invasive clinical procedures to insert or inject the drug delivery system and are associated with significant side effects themselves.  This project will investigate the potential of treating glaucoma with a noninvasive patient-administered eye drop that comfortably forms a gel in the area beneath the lower eyelid where it will provide up to one month of glaucoma medication.

column3: Combined Hydrogel/Microparticle Eye Drops for Sustained Delivery of Glaucoma Medication
column4: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE:  Glaucoma is the second leading cause of blindness worldwide with this prevalence expected to increase substantially in coming years as it is more common in elderly adults.  The most common and preferred treatment to slow or stop the progression of glaucoma is the self-administration of topical eye drop medication as many as three times a day.  Eye drops are a highly inefficient treatment method due to limited retention and absorption of drug patient compliance issues due to the frequent dosing and side effects resulting from high levels of drug needed to achieve therapeutic effects.  Current efforts to develop new sustained release formulations that provide controlled delivery of glaucoma drugs for days or weeks (avoiding the need for topical drops) require invasive clinical procedures to insert or inject the drug delivery system and are associated with significant side effects themselves.  This project will investigate the potential of treating glaucoma with a noninvasive patient-administered eye drop that comfortably forms a gel in the area beneath the lower eyelid where it will provide up to one month of glaucoma medication.

column3: Combined Hydrogel/Microparticle Eye Drops for Sustained Delivery of Glaucoma Medication
column4: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE:  Glaucoma is the second leading cause of blindness worldwide with this prevalence expected to increase substantially in coming years as it is more common in elderly adults.  The most common and preferred treatment to slow or stop the progression of glaucoma is the self-administration of topical eye drop medication as many as three times a day.  Eye drops are a highly inefficient treatment method due to limited retention and absorption of drug patient compliance issues due to the frequent dosing and side effects resulting from high levels of drug needed to achieve therapeutic effects.  Current efforts to develop new sustained release formulations that provide controlled delivery of glaucoma drugs for days or weeks (avoiding the need for topical drops) require invasive clinical procedures to insert or inject the drug delivery system and are associated with significant side effects themselves.  This project will investigate the potential of treating glaucoma with a noninvasive patient-administered eye drop that comfortably forms a gel in the area beneath the lower eyelid where it will provide up to one month of glaucoma medication.

column3: Mechanistic analysis of transport through the mucus barrier
column4: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE:  The surface properties of pathogenic viruses or drug delivery vehicles determine how fast they can penetrate the mucus barrier yet the critical parameters that govern their transport are poorly understood and not possible to predict. column3: Combined Hydrogel/Microparticle Eye Drops for Sustained Delivery of Glaucoma Medication
column4: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE:  Glaucoma is the second leading cause of blindness worldwide with this prevalence expected to increase substantially in coming years as it is more common in elderly adults.  The most common and preferred treatment to slow or stop the progression of glaucoma is the self-administration of topical eye drop medication as many as three times a day.  Eye drops are a highly inefficient treatment method due to limited retention and absorption of drug patient compliance issues due to the frequent dosing and side effects resulting from high levels of drug needed to achieve therapeutic effects.  Current efforts to develop new sustained release formulations that provide controlled delivery of glaucoma drugs for days or weeks (avoiding the need for topical drops) require invasive clinical procedures to insert or inject the drug delivery system and are associated with significant side effects themselves.  This project will investigate the potential of treating glaucoma with a noninvasive patient-administered eye drop that comfortably forms a gel in the area beneath the lower eyelid where it will provide up to one month of glaucoma medication.

Treatment involves repeated infusions of coagulation factor VIII throughout the life of the patient which creates tremendous discomfort and is extremely expensive. column3: Mechanistic analysis of transport through the mucus barrier
column4: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE:  The surface properties of pathogenic viruses or drug delivery vehicles determine how fast they can penetrate the mucus barrier yet the critical parameters that govern their transport are poorly understood and not possible to predict. The aims of this project are to predict whether a variety of synthetic or natural particles having complex physicalchemical and biological properties can pass through the mucus barrier in the body. This project will reveal molecular fingerprints that are diagnostic for fast and slow passage through mucus and will thereby significantly impact societal health by providing new strategies for preventing prevalent infectious diseases and for facilitating drug delivery.

column3: Development of a Biomimetic Vitreous Substitute
column4: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE:  The proposed research is relevant to public health because a biomimetic vitreous gel substitute would yield a much-needed alternative to non-physiological vitreous substitutes such as perfluorocarbons and silicone oils thus dramatically decreasing patient burden.  The vitreous gel plays a central role in the growth and overall health of the eye. To avoid the long-term deleterious effects of current materials it is critical that vitreous substitutes mimic the natural vitreous.  This project is in line with the underlying mission of theNIH since we seek to understand how the vitreous has been engineered in nature and will apply that understanding to the prevention or decrease of vision loss.

column3: Combined Hydrogel/Microparticle Eye Drops for Sustained Delivery of Glaucoma Medication
column4: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE:  Glaucoma is the second leading cause of blindness worldwide with this prevalence expected to increase substantially in coming years as it is more common in elderly adults.  The most common and preferred treatment to slow or stop the progression of glaucoma is the self-administration of topical eye drop medication as many as three times a day.  Eye drops are a highly inefficient treatment method due to limited retention and absorption of drug patient compliance issues due to the frequent dosing and side effects resulting from high levels of drug needed to achieve therapeutic effects.  Current efforts to develop new sustained release formulations that provide controlled delivery of glaucoma drugs for days or weeks (avoiding the need for topical drops) require invasive clinical procedures to insert or inject the drug delivery system and are associated with significant side effects themselves.  This project will investigate the potential of treating glaucoma with a noninvasive patient-administered eye drop that comfortably forms a gel in the area beneath the lower eyelid where it will provide up to one month of glaucoma medication.
